title: 天气与气候
lead: 「今天下雨」和「这里多雨」是两回事——一个是瞬间，一个是脾气。
leadEn: 'Raining today' and 'this place is rainy' are different things—one is a moment, one is a temperament.
west: 天气：短时刻的大气状态——气温、气压、湿度、风与降水的此刻组合，几天之外就难以预报。
westEn: Weather: the atmosphere's state right now—temperature, pressure, humidity, wind and precipitation in today's combination, unforecastable beyond a few days.
east: 气候：长期统计出来的脾气——三十年的天气平均与极值，勾勒出类型、季节与变化规律。
eastEn: Climate: the temperament averaged over decades—thirty years of weather statistics shaping type, seasonality and extremes.
bridge: 气候是天气的统计，一个暖冬不推翻趋势，一次寒潮也不。把瞬时当趋势、把趋势当挡箭牌，是同一类错误的两面。
bridgeEn: Climate is weather's statistics: one warm winter does not overturn a trend, nor does one cold snap. Mistaking a moment for the trend—and the trend for an excuse—are two faces of the same error.

title: 内力与外力
lead: 地表是谁的作品？一个力量搭骨架，一个力量做雕刻。
leadEn: Who sculpted the surface? One force builds the frame; the other does the carving.
west: 内力：地球自身能量驱动的造山、断裂、岩浆与变质——把地表抬高、撕开，制造高低差异。
westEn: Internal forces: mountain building, faulting, magma and metamorphism driven by the planet's own energy—lifting, tearing, and inventing relief.
east: 外力：太阳能与重力驱动的流水、风、冰川与波浪——削高填低，把差异一层层抹平。
eastEn: External forces: water, wind, ice and waves driven by sunlight and gravity—cutting highs, filling lows, smoothing the difference away.
bridge: 地貌是两者同一时刻的账单：青藏高原既在被抬升也在被剥蚀，谁赢就看时窗多长。内力定大势，外力定细节。
bridgeEn: A landform is both forces' ledger at one moment: the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau rises and is stripped at once—who wins depends on the time window. Internals set the stage; externals set the detail.

title: 夏季风与冬季风
lead: 同一套海陆温差机制，夏冬两季几乎把风向往反方向各吹一次。
leadEn: One land-sea heating mechanism, blowing the wind almost backwards in summer versus winter.
west: 夏季风：大陆升温快形成低压，风从海洋吹向陆地，带来丰沛水汽与雨带——雨热同期是农业的厚礼。
westEn: Summer monsoon: the fast-heating continent drops pressure and air flows sea-to-land, hauling moisture and the rain belt—rain and heat together, a gift to farming.
east: 冬季风：大陆冷却快形成高压，风从内陆吹向海洋，干冷少雨——同一片土地的另一副面孔。
eastEn: Winter monsoon: the quick-cooling continent turns high-pressure and air flows land-to-sea, dry and cold—this same land's other face.
bridge: 两季风是同一条热力环流的两个挡位：海陆温差换向，风向随之倒转。季风区的旱涝，多半在夏季风进退的早晚强弱里找原因。
bridgeEn: The two seasons are one heat engine in two gears: when the land-sea temperature gap flips, the wind flips. A monsoon land's floods and droughts are mostly written in the monsoon's timing and strength.

title: 暖流与寒流
lead: 海上的两条传送带，一条从赤道搬运温暖，一条从深处带上冷与养分。
leadEn: Two conveyor belts at sea: one ferries warmth from the equator, one lifts cold and nutrients from the deep.
west: 暖流：从低纬流向高纬的温水——增温增湿，让西欧的冬天比同纬度温和得多。
westEn: Warm currents: water moving from low to high latitude—warming and moistening the air above, making western Europe's winters far milder than its latitude suggests.
east: 寒流：从高纬或深海上涌的冷水——降温减湿，冷却过的空气压不住水汽，西岸沙漠因此贴海而生。
eastEn: Cold currents: water sinking from high latitude or welling from the deep—chilling and drying the air, so western-coast deserts hug the sea.
bridge: 寒流的「上升流」把海底养分带上来的地方，正是渔场最密集之处——减湿的代价换来了另一重馈赠。两条流在大洋东西岸方向相反，是环流的镜像。
bridgeEn: Where cold currents upwell nutrients from the seabed, the great fisheries bloom—the desert's price paid in another gift. The two currents run in opposite directions on opposite sides of an ocean: the gyre seen in mirror.

title: 厄尔尼诺与拉尼娜
lead: 同一片热带太平洋的「发烧」与「着凉」——一对跷跷板的两端，名字却都来自圣诞前后。
leadEn: Fever and chills in the same tropical Pacific—two ends of a seesaw, both named around Christmas.
west: 厄尔尼诺：东南信风减弱，暖水堆回中东太平洋，海温异常升高——秘鲁渔场减产，全球雨带重新洗牌。
westEn: El Niño: the trade winds slacken, warm water sloshes back east, the sea runs hot—the Peru fishery thins and the world's rain belts are reshuffled.
east: 拉尼娜：信风偏强，暖水被更狠地推向西太平洋，东太平洋异常冷——往往对应更强的台风季与另一套旱涝格局。
eastEn: La Niña: trades strengthen, warm water is pushed harder westward, the east runs cold—often a livelier typhoon season and a different map of wet and dry.
bridge: 两者是同一耦合系统（海洋与大气互相喂养）的正负位相，并非轮流出现的两种病。预报员盯的是「位相与强度」，不是善恶标签。
bridgeEn: Both are the positive and negative phases of one coupled system—ocean and air feeding each other—not two illnesses on rotation. Forecasters track phase and strength, not good or evil.

title: 高原与盆地
lead: 都是「大地形」，一个抬高世界屋脊，一个兜住一方天地。
leadEn: Both are grand shapes: one raises the roof of the world, one cups its own little universe.
west: 高原：大面积抬升、顶面相对平坦的高地——海拔高、气温低、空气稀薄，冰川与冻土是常客。
westEn: Plateau: a broad uplifted highland with a relatively flat top—high, cold, thin air; glaciers and permafrost are regulars.
east: 盆地：四周高、中间低的闭合洼地——从塔里木到刚果盆地，气候随纬度与封闭程度千差万别。
eastEn: Basin: enclosed lowland ringed by heights—from the Tarim to the Congo, its climate swings with latitude and how sealed it is.
bridge: 两者可以嵌套：青藏高原上就有柴达木盆地。抬升与沉降、蓄水与漏水，往往在同一张图上并存，别把地形类别当互斥抽屉。
bridgeEn: They nest: the Qaidam Basin sits inside the Tibetan Plateau itself. Uplift and subsidence, impounding and leaking coexist on one map—landform classes are not exclusive drawers.

title: 河流上游与下游
lead: 同一条河，在山里是雕刻刀，到平原是搬运工——角色随坡度换人。
leadEn: One river, two jobs: sculptor in the mountains, hauler on the plain—the slope re-casts the role.
west: 上游：坡陡流急，以下切与溯源侵蚀为主——V 形谷、瀑布、急滩，河床堆着大块砾石。
westEn: Upper course: steep and fast, cutting down and headward—V-valleys, waterfalls, rapids, and coarse gravel on the bed.
east: 下游：坡缓流慢，以侧蚀与堆积为主——河道弯曲、泥沙铺出平原与三角洲，河床越垫越高。
eastEn: Lower course: gentle and slow, widening and depositing—meanders, silty floodplains and deltas, a bed that lifts itself.
bridge: 上游的「破坏」就是下游的「建设」：泥沙被水一路搬运，把山削出的高度在入海处补回来。分水与肥力，是同一条河的两笔账。
bridgeEn: The upper course's destruction is the lower course's construction: sediment carries mountain height down to rebuild it at the mouth. Erosion and fertility are one river's two ledgers.

title: 城市气候与乡村气候
lead: 同一纬度，城市比郊外更热、更浊、有时更会下雨——差异全是人造的。
leadEn: Same latitude, but the city runs hotter, hazier and often wetter—every difference is man-made.
west: 城市：不透水地面与蓄热建材白天存热夜里释放，加上人为排热与微粒，形成热岛、浊岛与额外的对流雨。
westEn: City: impervious surfaces and heat-hoarding materials store daylight and exhale at night; added waste heat and aerosols build the heat island, the haze island and extra convective rain.
east: 乡村：植被与土壤蒸腾散热，夜间辐射降温干脆利落——温差大、空气净、降水回归天气系统本身。
eastEn: Countryside: plants and soil cool by evapotranspiration, and clear nights shed heat fast—bigger day-night swings, cleaner air, rain left to the weather systems themselves.
bridge: 热岛是叠加在本地气候上的人为小气候：规划里的通风廊道、绿地与水体系，就是把乡村的散热机制请回城市。
bridgeEn: The heat island is a man-made microclimate riding on the local one: ventilation corridors, green space and water in planning are the countryside's cooling tricks invited back into town.

title: 节气与气象四季
lead: 一套按太阳位置切二十四个刻度，一套按实际温度画候——同一个地球的两把季节尺。
leadEn: One ruler slices the Sun's path into 24 marks; the other reads the thermometer's seasons—the planet measured by two sticks.
west: 二十四节气：把黄道分成 24 段，定在太阳位置的几何刻度上——哪天直射哪条纬线清清楚楚，千年不变。
westEn: The 24 solar terms: the ecliptic cut into 24 spans fixed to the Sun's geometry—exact latitude of overhead Sun per date, unchanged for a millennium.
east: 气象季节：按滑动均温切分入春入冬的门槛——同一节气在岭南与东北对应完全不同的地面温度。
eastEn: Meteorological seasons: spring and winter declared by rolling-mean temperature thresholds—the same term means wildly different ground truth in Guangzhou versus Heilongjiang.
bridge: 节气是「天时」，物候是「地表的回执」：两者错位不是谁错了，而是轨道几何与地方热状态本就分账计算。最热不在夏至、最冷不在冬至，延迟同样是这条线索。
bridgeEn: Terms are heaven's clock; phenology is the ground's receipt. The mismatch isn't error—orbital geometry and local heat keep separate books. Peak heat not at summer's height, peak cold not at winter's depth: the lag is the same thread.

title: 时区与夏令时
lead: 时区是官方对太阳的粗对齐，夏令时是夏天再拨一小时的微调——一年一争议。
leadEn: Time zones are the official rough alignment with the Sun; daylight saving nudges another hour in summer—a yearly argument.
west: 时区：以经度为基础的制度切割，一国一区便于铁路与行政——但几何上每 15° 才该换一小时。
westEn: Time zones: longitude-based institutional cuts—one zone per country for railways and paperwork—though geometry asks an hour per 15°.
east: 夏令时：夏季把钟拨快一小时，让作息多借一段傍晚天光，代价是换日之夜的混乱与跨界协调成本。
eastEn: Daylight saving: spring the clock forward an hour to borrow more evening daylight, paying with the disoriented transition night and cross-border friction.
bridge: 两者都承认一个事实：制度时刻与太阳时刻永远有缝隙。纬度越高、经度越偏的角落缝隙越大——中国新疆的「作息晚两小时」就是这道缝的日常显影。
bridgeEn: Both confess one fact: clock time and solar time keep a gap—widest at high latitude and far longitude. Xinjiang's two-hours-later daily schedule is that seam made visible.

title: 喀斯特与雅丹
lead: 一个是水溶出来的迷宫，一个是风吹出的舰队——同样刻在沉积岩上，工具完全相反。
leadEn: One a maze dissolved by water, one a fleet carved by wind—both cut into sedimentary rock with opposite tools.
west: 喀斯特：湿润区的水与二氧化碳联手溶蚀石灰岩——石林、峰丛、溶洞、地下河，地表缺水、地下成网。
westEn: Karst: damp water and carbon dioxide dissolve limestone—stone forests, tower fields, caves and underground rivers; the surface thirsts while a subterranean net flows.
east: 雅丹：干旱区的风借沙粒磨蚀湖相泥岩——垄槽相间的风蚀舰队，只属于曾经有湖、如今有风的荒漠。
eastEn: Yardang: dry wind sanded across lacustrine mud—ridges and trenches like a fleet; it belongs only to deserts that once held lakes and now hold wind.
bridge: 两者都是「岩石 + 介质 + 气候带」的配方产物：把雅丹搬到湿润区、喀斯特搬到荒漠，都刻不成形。地貌是气候写给岩石的字。
bridgeEn: Both are recipes of rock + agent + climate zone: transplant yardang into damp land or karst into desert and neither sculpts. Landforms are climates' handwriting on rock.

title: 三角洲与冲积扇
lead: 同是河流撒手的瞬间堆出的扇形——一个撒进海里，一个撒在山口。
leadEn: Both are fans piled the moment a river lets go—one into the sea, one at the mountain's door.
west: 三角洲：入海（湖）处流速骤降加海水顶托，泥沙在水下铺出向海倾没的平原——河口分汆、岸线向前爬。
westEn: Delta: at the sea (or lake), flow collapses and the standing water checks the current—sill spreads a seaward-dipping plain, distributies braiding, shoreline creeping outward.
east: 冲积扇：出山口坡度骤缓，携沙能力断崖式下跌，泥沙在山麓铺出一把向山下展开的扇——扇顶粗、扇缘细。
eastEn: Alluvial fan: leaving the gorge, slope collapses and carry capacity falls off a cliff—sediment unfurls downhill-fanning from the apron, coarse at the head, fine at the rim.
bridge: 都是「流速丢失仪式」的沉积物签名，只是丢失原因不同：一个输给静止水体，一个输给地形换坡。分选规律也同源：粗粒先落地，细粒走更远。
bridgeEn: Both are sediment signatures of a speed-loss ceremony, different only in cause: one loses to standing water, one to changing slope. The sorting law is shared—coarse lands first, fine travels farther.

title: 冰川地貌与河流地貌
lead: 冰与水都在雕刻地表：冰拖着碎石前行，水携着泥沙奔流——两者造出的谷地有时一眼难分。
leadEn: Both ice and water carve the surface — ice dragging its rubble, water carrying its silt — and the valleys they leave can look startlingly alike.
west: 冰川刨蚀出横剖面呈 U 形的幽谷，谷壁陡、谷底平，把碎石成片推成侧碛与终碛，还常将河道搅得七拐八弯，留下羊背石与冰斗。
westEn: Glacial ice gouges U-shaped valleys — steep walls, a flattened floor — shoving rubble into lateral and terminal moraines, snubbing streams into confused bends, and leaving roche-moutonnee and cirques.
east: 河流以下切与侧蚀为主：幼年切出 V 形深谷，壮年摆出曲流与河漫滩，入海处堆成三角洲——泥沙分选好，颗粒随流速递变。
eastEn: A river cuts down and undercuts sideways: youth carves a V-shaped gorge, maturity swings into meanders and floodplains, and at the mouth it builds a delta — well-sorted sediment grading with the current.
bridge: 判谷先看剖面：U 形多归冰川、V 形多归河流；但许多山谷是「先冰后河」接力雕成，只看一面易认错。两者都是侵蚀—搬运—堆积三步曲，只是主角交替。
bridgeEn: Read the cross-section first: U says glacier, V says river — yet many valleys were carved relay-style, ice then water, so judging by one actor misreads them. Both run the same three-step cycle of erosion, transport and deposition, with the lead role passing on.

title: 气旋与反气旋
lead: 同一张等压线图，中心是低气压还是高气压，决定了空气往上抽还是往下压，也就决定了阴雨还是晴好。
leadEn: On the same pressure map, whether the centre is low or high decides whether air is drawn upward or pressed down — and whether you get rain or clear skies.
west: 气旋是低压系统：四周空气向心辐合、被迫上升，冷却凝结成云致雨，台风与温带气旋皆属此列，北半球气流呈逆时针旋入。
westEn: A cyclone is a low: air converges inward and is forced to rise, cooling and condensing into cloud and rain — typhoons and mid-latitude lows alike, spinning counter-clockwise in the northern hemisphere.
east: 反气旋是高压系统：中心空气下沉、向四周幅散，下沉增温使云消雨歇，多为晴燥天气，夏季伏旱与冬季冷高压都由它主导。
eastEn: An anticyclone is a high: air subsides at the centre and spreads outward, and the sinking warms and dries it, clearing the clouds — persistently fair, as in summer droughts and winter cold highs.
bridge: 风总是由高压吹向低压、又被地转偏向力扳弯；气旋与反气旋像一对咬合的齿轮，一个抽气成雨、一个压气放晴，共同驱动中纬度的天气更替。
bridgeEn: Wind always blows from high toward low, bent askew by the Coriolis effect; cyclone and anticyclone mesh like two gears — one pulling air into rain, one pressing air into clear — together turning the mid-latitude weather machine.

title: 岩浆岩与沉积岩
lead: 三大类岩石里，一个来自炽热岩浆的冷却结晶，一个来自碎屑与化学沉淀的层层压实——形成方式几乎相反。
leadEn: Of the great rock families, one condenses from molten fire, one is pressed from debris and chemical ooze — near-opposite ways of forming.
west: 岩浆岩由岩浆冷却结晶而成：侵入地壳深处缓冷则晶粒粗大如花冈岩，喷出地表急冷则细密乃至成玻璃质；追溯到底，一切母岩都源自它。
westEn: Igneous rock crystallises from cooling magma: intruded deep and cooled slowly it grows coarse grains like granite, erupted and chilled fast it turns fine or even glassy; every rock's ancestor traces back to it.
east: 沉积岩由风化搬运的碎屑、生物残骸或化学沉淀在地表逐层堆积、压实胶结而成，常具层理、可能含化石，是记录地球历史的书页。
eastEn: Sedimentary rock forms as weathered debris, shells or chemical precipitates pile up layer by layer at the surface and are compacted and cemented — often bedded, often fossil-bearing, the pages of Earth's history.
bridge: 在岩石循环里两者可互转：岩浆岩被风化剥蚀变成沉积岩，沉积岩若被埋到深处高温熔融又能重生成岩浆岩；变质岩则是二者受热受压的第三条路。
bridgeEn: In the rock cycle they convert into each other: igneous weathers into sedimentary, and sedimentary buried to melting heat is reborn as igneous; metamorphic rock is the third path, both cooked by heat and pressure.

title: 城市化与逆城市化
lead: 人口向城市聚集，与人口从城市中心向外回流：一个把乡变成城，一个看似退城，其实多半是城市在摊大饼、重组。
leadEn: People crowding into cities, and people flowing back out of the core — one turns village into town; the other, though it looks like a retreat, is usually a city spreading and reorganising.
west: 城市化是人口与经济活动向城市集中、城市人口比重持续上升的过程，多伴随工业化，先表现为郊区被并入、城市数量与规模齐增。
westEn: Urbanization is the concentration of people and activity in cities, the urban share of population rising — mostly driven by industry, first swallowing suburbs then swelling both the number and size of towns.
east: 逆城市化是发达城市人口向郊区、乡村与小城镇回流的现象，源于中心城区拥挤、地价高企与交通通信普及，并非城市衰落，而是人口分布的再疏解。
eastEn: Counter-urbanization is the drift of people out of dense core cities to suburbs, villages and small towns — born of congestion and high land prices and made possible by cars and networks; not the city dying but its population spreading again.
bridge: 两者常是同一城市化进程的不同阶段：先集聚、再外溢，形成城市群与都市带。判断当下处在哪一段，要看人口是流向单个大城市，还是流向它周边一圈卫星城。
bridgeEn: The two are often stages of one process — concentration first, then spillover, building city-regions and corridors. To see which stage you're in, ask whether people pour into a single great city or into a ring of satellites around it.
